title: Gravitational pull shrinks with the square of the distance
summary: The gravitational force between two bodies is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
body: OpenStax Physics states that the gravitational force is directly proportional to the product of the two masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them. Doubling the distance, on that rule, cuts the force to a quarter, not merely to a half. NASA Space Place says only that gravity gets weaker with distance, without the square. This card is the textbook's square rule. Urone and Hinrichs, 26 March 2020.
